page: Microsoft Azure E64_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Ev5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes hyper-threading with 2.0 threads per core, a 105 MB L3 cache, and support for AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU and memory scores. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth are also in the top 25%, alongside high throughput for static web serving and database operations. However, single-core performance, single-threaded compression, and Redis SET operations fall within the average range. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in large-scale language model execution; while prompt processing for a 70B model is average, text generation for the same model is weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64_v5 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads without the added expense of local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators. The high memory capacity combined with strong multi-core execution makes this instance highly suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching, enterprise applications, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E64_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Ev5 family, powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores), 512.0 GB of RAM, and a 105 MB L3 cache, with no local storage or GPUs. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, it delivers strong multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and excellent database operations. While single-core tasks and large-model text generation show average to weak performance, its high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for large databases, multi-threaded data processing, and enterprise workloads.
